label: conjecture
title: Conjecture
body_md:
\label{conjecture}
Let $X\to S$ be an affine family of normal varieties, and let $S'\subseteq S$ be a Zariski-dense subset of closed points such that $X_s$ is of klt type. Suppose $\eta\in S$ is the generic point. Then, $X_{\overline{\eta}}$ is of klt type.
head: environment

label: Mallory
title: Conjecture
body_md:
\label{Mallory}
Let $X:=\operatorname{Spec} R$ be an lc type affine variety, and assume $\mathcal{O}_X$ is $\mathcal{D}_X$-simple. Then, $X$ is of klt type.
head: environment

label: simple
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{simple}
Let $X\to S$ be an affine family of normal varieties, and let $S'\subseteq S$ be a Zariski-dense subset of closed points such that $X_s$ is of klt type. Suppose $\eta\in S$ is the generic point, and assume $\mathcal{O}_{X_{\overline{\eta}}}$ is $\mathcal{D}_{X_{\overline{\eta}}}$-simple. Then, $X_{\overline{\eta}}$ is of klt type.
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $X$ be a variety. A \emph{differential operator} $P:\mathcal{O}_X\to \mathcal{O}_X$ of order $r$ is a $\mathbb{C}$-linear map such that for all local sections $g\in \mathcal{O}_X$, the map $s\mapsto D(gs)-gD(s)$ is a differential operator of order $r-1$. For the base case $r=0$, we define a differential operator of order $0$ to be an $\mathcal{O}_X$-linear map. We can define $\mathcal{D}_X$ as an $\mathcal{O}_X$-module such that for every affine $U\subseteq X$,
$$ \mathcal{D}_X(U):=\{P\mid P:\mathcal{O}_U\to \mathcal{O}_U\text{ is a differential operator}\}.$$
head: environment

label: hyogok
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{hyogok}
Let $(X,\Delta)$ be a couple. We say that $(X,\Delta)$ is \emph{of klt type} if there exists an effective $\mathbb{Q}$-Weil divisor $\Delta'$ on $X$ such that $(X,\Delta+\Delta')$ is klt.
head: environment

title: Definition
head: environment

label: daljeonjeosuji
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{daljeonjeosuji}
Let $(X,\Delta)$ be a klt pair, and let $\mathfrak{a}\subsetneq \mathcal{O}_X$ be an ideal. Then, there exists a Kollár component computing $\mathrm{lct}(X,\Delta;\mathfrak{a})$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $T$ be a prime divisor computing $\mathrm{lct}(X,\Delta;\mathfrak{a})$, and let $x\in X$ be the generic point of an irreducible component of the center of $T$.

\smallskip

We can substitute $\mathfrak{a}$ by $\mathfrak{a}_x+\mathfrak{m}^N_x$ with $N\cdot \mathrm{ord}_T(\mathfrak{m}_x)\ge \mathrm{ord}_T(\mathfrak{a})$. Indeed, since
$$ \mathrm{ord}_T(\mathfrak{a}_x+\mathfrak{m}^N_x)=\min\{\mathrm{ord}_T(\mathfrak{a}),N\cdot \mathrm{ord}_T(\mathfrak{m}_x)\}=\mathrm{ord}_T(\mathfrak{a}),$$
we obtain
$$ c:=\mathrm{lct}(X,\Delta;\mathfrak{a})\le \mathrm{lct}(X_x,\Delta_x;\mathfrak{a}_x+\mathfrak{m}^N_x)\le \frac{A_{X_x,\Delta_x}(T)}{\mathrm{ord}_T(\mathfrak{a}_x+\mathfrak{m}^N_x)}=\mathrm{lct}(X,\Delta;\mathfrak{a}).$$

\smallskip

Now, apply \cite[Lemma 2.7]{Xu20}. Then, there exists a Kollár component $S$ over $X$ such that
$$ A_{X_x,\Delta_x}(S)=c\cdot \mathrm{ord}_S(\mathfrak{a}_x+\mathfrak{m}^N_x)\le c\cdot \mathrm{ord}_S(\mathfrak{a}_x)\le A_{X_x,\Delta_x}(S),$$
and hence, $A_{X,\Delta}(S)=c\cdot \mathrm{ord}_S(\mathfrak{a})$.
head: environment

label: Kollar
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
First of all, we treat the case of $\kappa(x)=\mathbb{C}$. For the case of $S\subseteq X$, we obtain $A_X(S)=1$ and $\mathrm{ord}_S(Pf)\ge \mathrm{ord}_S(f)-r$ by direct computation. Hence, we may assume that $S$ is not on $X$.

\smallskip

We will follow the argument in \cite[Theorem 5.10]{XZ26b}. The main idea is that we can translate the problem of proving (\ref{ineq}) into the problem of computing the maximal slope of a symmetric power of a tangent bundle. The difference is that \cite{XZ26b} uses $\Omega^{[j]}_{\mathcal{X}'}(\log \mathcal{S})|_{\mathcal{S}}$ because it is treating differential \emph{forms}, while we use $\mathrm{Sym}^{[j]}_{\mathcal{S}}T_{\mathcal{S}}$ because we are treating differential \emph{operators}.

\smallskip

\noindent \textbf{Step 1.} Let $\pi:(X',S)\to X$ be the plt extraction of $S$. By adjunction, there exists $\Delta_S$ on $S$ such that
$$ (K_{X'}+S)|_S=K_S+\Delta_S\,\text{ and }(S,\Delta_S)\text{ is log Fano.}$$
Set $H:=-(K_S+\Delta_S)$. Then, $H$ is ample. Since $K_{X'}+S=\pi^*K_X+A_X(S)S$, restriction to $S$ gives 
\begin{equation} \label{H}
H\sim_{\mathbb{Q}} -A_X(S)S|_S.
\end{equation}
Here, we have shrunk $X$ around $x$ so that a Cartier multiple of $K_X$ is linearly trivial.

\smallskip

Consider the index-one covering stack associated with $S$: $\rho:\mathcal{X}'\to X',\,\mathcal{S}:=\rho^*S$ (cf. \cite[Definition 5.3.1]{AH11}). The divisor $\mathcal{S}$ is Cartier. There is a smooth open substack $\mathcal{U}\subseteq \mathcal{X}'$ such that $S^{\circ}:=\mathcal{S}\cap \mathcal{U}$ is smooth and $\operatorname{codim}_{\mathcal{S}}(\mathcal{S}\setminus \mathcal{S}^{\circ})\ge 2$.

\smallskip

Let us explain why we use an index-one cover in the sense of a \emph{stack}, rather than merely an index-one covering that renders $\mathcal{S}$ Cartier. If we only work with an index-one cover as a \emph{scheme}, we can show that $X$ admits an open cover $\{U_i\}$ such that each $U_i$ has an index-one covering scheme $U'_i\to U_i$. However, to glue the $U'_i$ together globally, we need the framework of (Deligne–Mumford) stacks.

\smallskip

Define $\mathcal{I}:=\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{U}}(-\mathcal{S}^{\circ})$ and $\mathcal{N}:=\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{X}'}(\mathcal{S})|_{\mathcal{S}}$. Then, $\mathcal{N}$ is the normal line bundle on the index stack. Let $h:W\overset{\tau}{\to} \mathcal{S}\overset{\rho}{\to}S$ be a finite cover that factors through $\mathcal{S}$. Then, (\ref{H}) gives 
\begin{equation} \label{yanghak}
\begin{aligned}
\deg_H \mathcal{N}:=\frac{c_1(\tau^*\mathcal{N})\cdot (h^*H)^{n-2}}{\deg \tau}=-\frac{\deg \rho}{A_X(S)}H^{n-1}.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}

\smallskip

\noindent \textbf{Step 2.} In this step, we move our differential operator $P$ to $\mathcal{S}^{\circ}$, and to $\mathcal{S}$.

\smallskip

By localization and étale pullback, $P$ defines a rational differential operator on $\mathcal{U}$, of order at most $r$, regular away from $\mathcal{S}^{\circ}$. On an étale chart $\operatorname{Spec} A$, choose coordinates adapted to $\mathcal{S}^{\circ}=(t=0)$ and $b\ge 0$ such that $t^bP$ is regular. Then, the expression of $P$ using the local coordinate on $A$ gives
$$ P(t^mA)\subseteq t^{m-b-r}A \text{ for }m\ge 0$$
(cf. \cite[Proposition 1.4.6]{Yek92}). Hence, we obtain that there exists an integer $q\ge 0$ such that \begin{equation}\label{P}
P(\mathcal{I}^m)\subseteq \mathcal{I}^{m-q}\text{ for }m \ge 0.
\end{equation}
Choose $q$ as a minimum. If $q=0$, the desired inequality follows immediately. Otherwise, $P$ induces maps
$$ D_m:\mathcal{I}^m/\mathcal{I}^{m+1}\to \mathcal{I}^{m-q}/\mathcal{I}^{m-q+1}, $$
one of which is nonzero by the minimality of $q$. Fix such an $m$. Using $\mathcal{I}^k/\mathcal{I}^{k+1}\cong \mathcal{N}^{-k}|_{\mathcal{S}^{\circ}}$, we thus obtain a nonzero differential operator $D_m:\mathcal{N}^{-m}|_{\mathcal{S}^{\circ}}\to \mathcal{N}^{q-m}|_{\mathcal{S}^{\circ}}$ of order $j\le r$.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

\smallskip

                                                                
                          
                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        

           

                                                                                                                                                  
                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                               

           

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         

           

                                                                                                                                                                                                        

           

                                                         
                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            

           

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           

           

Since $\mathcal{S}^{\circ}$ is smooth and $D_m$ has order $j$, its principal symbol gives a non-zero section
$$ 0\ne s\in H^0\left(\mathcal{S}^{\circ},\mathrm{Sym}^{j}T_{\mathcal{S}^{\circ}}\otimes \mathcal{N}^q|_{\mathcal{S}^{\circ}}\right)$$
(cf. \cite[(11.1.4)]{HTT08} with $\mathcal{V}=\mathcal{N}^{-m}|_{\mathcal{S}^{\circ}}\oplus \mathcal{N}^{q-m}|_{\mathcal{S}^{\circ}}$). Reflexifying this gives
\begin{equation}\label{nonzero}
0\ne s \in H^0\left(\mathcal{S},\mathrm{Sym}^{[j]}T_{\mathcal{S}}\otimes \mathcal{N}^q|_{\mathcal{S}}\right).
\end{equation}

           

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       

           

                                                                                                                                                                                
                                                            
                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                         
                                                            
                                                                                                
                                                              
                                                                                                       

           

                                                                                                                                                
                              
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
    
                
                         
                                    
                         
                          
              
   
                                                                                                                                                   

           

                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                 
                 
                                               
                        
                                                                                                                                                                                              
               
                                                                                                                                                                             

           

                                                            
                                                                                                                           
                        
                                 
                                                                                                             
               

           

\noindent \textbf{Step 3.} In this step, we compute the maximal slope of $\mathrm{Sym}^{[j]}T_{\mathcal{S}}\otimes \mathcal{N}^{-q}|_{\mathcal{S}}$ and reduce the inequality (\ref{ineq}) to the computation of the slope. Let $h:W\overset{\tau}{\to} \mathcal{S}\overset{\rho}{\to} S$ be a cover that factors through $\mathcal{S}$ as in Step 1.

\smallskip

On $\mathcal{S}^{\circ}$, put $\mathcal{C}^{\circ}:=\Omega^1_{\mathcal{U}}(\log \mathcal{S}^{\circ})|_{\mathcal{S}^{\circ}}$. Then, we obtain
$$ 0\to \Omega^1_{\mathcal{S}^{\circ}}\to \mathcal{C}^{\circ} \to \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{S}^{\circ}}\to 0 $$
and
\begin{equation} \label{sm2}
0\to \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{S}^{\circ}}\to (\mathcal{C}^{\circ})^{\vee}\to T_{\mathcal{S}^{\circ}}\to 0.
\end{equation}
Let $\imath:\mathcal{S}^{\circ}\hookrightarrow \mathcal{S}$ be the inclusion, and let $\mathcal{C}:=\imath_*\mathcal{C}^{\circ}$. We obtain that by \cite[Lemma 5.5, 5.6 and 5.9]{XZ26b},
\begin{equation} \label{XuZhuang}
\mu_{\mathrm{max},\rho^*H}(\mathcal{C})\le -\frac{\min\{1,\delta(S,\Delta_S)\}}{n}H^{n-1}<0.
\end{equation}
Here, $\delta(S,\Delta_S)$ is the $\delta$-invariant in K-stability (for the definition, see \cite{FO18} and \cite{BJ20}), and we define $\mu_{\mathrm{max},\rho^*H}$ and $\mu_{\mathrm{min},\rho^*H}$ for a stack as in \cite[Definition 5.7, Proof of Theorem 5.10]{XZ26b}. Dualizing gives $\mu_{\mathrm{min},\rho^*H}(\mathcal{C}^{\vee})>0$. Since $T_{\mathcal{S}}$ is a quotient of $\mathcal{C}^{\vee}$ in codimension $1$, (\ref{sm2}) implies 
\begin{equation}\label{remaining}
\mu_{\mathrm{min},\rho^*H}(T_{\mathcal{S}})>0
\end{equation}

\smallskip

Let us prove $\mathrm{deg}_{\rho^*H} T_{\mathcal{S}}=H^{n-1}$. Indeed, Since $K_{\mathcal{S}}\sim_{\mathbb{Q}}\rho^*(K_S+\Delta_S)$ (cf. \cite[Proof of Lemma 5.6]{XZ26b}), we obtain that $c_1(T_{\mathcal{S}})\equiv \rho^*H$. Hence, pulling it back gives $c_1((\tau^*T_{\mathcal{S}})^{**})\equiv h^*H$. Thus, by \cite[Definition 5.7]{XZ26b},
$$ 
\begin{aligned}
\deg_{h^*H}((\tau^*T_{\mathcal{S}})^{**}) & =c_1((\tau^*T_{\mathcal{S}})^{**})\cdot (h^*H)^{n-2}
\\ &=(h^*H)^{n-1}
\\ &=(\deg h)H^{n-1}.
\end{aligned}$$

\smallskip

Let the Harder-Narasimhan factors of $(\tau^*T_{\mathcal{S}})^{**}$ have rank $e_i$ and slopes $\lambda_1>\cdots>\lambda_k$. By $\mu_{\mathrm{min},\rho^*H}(T_{\mathcal{S}})>0$, every $\lambda_i$ is positive. Therefore,
$$ (\deg \rho)H^{n-1}=\sum^k_{i=1}e_i\frac{1}{\deg \tau}\lambda_i\ge \frac{1}{\deg \tau}\lambda_1=\frac{1}{\deg \tau}\mu_{\mathrm{max},h^*H}((\tau^*T_{\mathcal{S}})^{**})=\mu_{\mathrm{max},H}(T_{\mathcal{S}}),$$
The slope inequality (cf. \cite[Theorem 4.2]{GKP16}) with the definition of slope for stacks consequently yields 
$$\mu_{\mathrm{max},\rho^*H}(\mathrm{Sym}^{[j]}T_{\mathcal{S}})\le j\cdot \deg \rho\cdot H^{n-1}.$$

\smallskip

The non-zero section (\ref{nonzero}) gives an injection
$$ \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{S}}\hookrightarrow \mathrm{Sym}^{[j]}T_{\mathcal{S}}\otimes \mathcal{N}^q|_{\mathcal{S}}.$$
Hence, the target has a maximal slope of at least zero. Therefore, we get
$$
\begin{aligned}
0& \le \mu_{\mathrm{max},\rho^*H}\left(\mathrm{Sym}^{[j]}T_{\mathcal{S}}\otimes \mathcal{N}^q|_{\mathcal{S}}\right)
\\ &=\mu_{\mathrm{max},\rho^*H}(\mathrm{Sym}^{[j]}T_{\mathcal{S}})+q\deg_H \mathcal{N}|_{\mathcal{S}} & (1)
\\ &\le \deg \rho\cdot \left(j-\frac{q}{A_X(S)}\right)H^{n-1},
\end{aligned}
$$
here we used (\ref{yanghak}) in (1). Since $H^{n-1},\deg \rho>0$, it follows that $q\le jA_X(S)\le rA_X(S)$. Finally, at the generic point of $\mathcal{S}$, the pullback of $f$ belongs to $\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{ord}_S(f)}$. Thus, (\ref{P}) gives 
$$\mathrm{ord}_S(Pf)\ge \mathrm{ord}_S(f)-q\ge \mathrm{ord}_S(f)-rA_X(S).$$
We complete the proof for the case of $\kappa(x)=\mathbb{C}$.

\smallskip

\noindent \textbf{Step 4.} Let us prove the case that $\kappa(x)\ne \mathbb{C}$. Put $K:=\overline{\kappa(x)}$. The argument of Step 3 applies to each irreducible component of $\mathcal{S}_K$ over $K\cong \mathbb{C}$. Hence, by \cite[Theorem 1.3.7]{HL10}, we obtain
                                                                                 
                                                                                                      
                    
\begin{equation} \label{remaining2}
\mu_{\mathrm{min},\rho^*H}(T_{\mathcal{S}/\kappa(x)})>0.
\end{equation}
                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
    
                                                                                                                              
   
       
                                                                             
      
                                                                                                       
                                                        

\smallskip

On $\mathcal{S}^{\circ}$, we have an exact sequence
\begin{equation} \label{remaining3}
0\to T_{\mathcal{S}^{\circ}/\kappa(x)}\to T_{\mathcal{S}^{\circ}/\mathbb{C}}\to \mathcal{O}_{S^{\circ}}\otimes_{\kappa(x)}\mathrm{Der}_{\mathbb{C}}(\kappa(x))\to 0 
\end{equation}
(cf. \cite[Lemma 04B2]{Stacks}). After reflexive extension, we obtain that
$$ 0\to T_{S/\kappa(x)}\to T_{\mathcal{S}/\mathbb{C}}\to \mathcal{D}\to 0 $$
with $\mathcal{D}^{**}=\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{S}}\otimes_{\kappa(x)}\mathrm{Der}_{\mathbb{C}}(\kappa(x))$. Hence, whenever $\mathcal{D}\ne 0$, it is semistable of slope zero.  It follows from (\ref{remaining2}) that
$$ \mu_{\mathrm{min},\rho^*H}(T_{\mathcal{S}/\mathbb{C}})\ge 0.$$
Moreover, by (\ref{remaining3}), $c_1(T_{\mathcal{S}/\mathbb{C}})=c_1(T_{\mathcal{S}/\kappa(x)})\equiv \rho^*H.$
We can see $K_{\mathcal{S}/\mathbb{C}}\sim_{\mathbb{Q}}\rho^*(K_{S/\mathbb{C}}+\Delta_S)$ 
(cf. \cite[Proof of Lemma 5.6]{XZ26b}).

\smallskip

                                                                                                  
                                                                         
                  
   
                
                                                                                        
          
                
By the same argument as in Step 3,
$$ \deg_{\rho^*H}T_{\mathcal{S}/\mathbb{C}}=\deg_{\rho^*H}T_{\mathcal{S}/\kappa(x)}=H^{n-1}.$$
We can proceed with the argument in Step 3 to prove the desired inequality.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
By the same argument, we expect that we can improve the inequality in Lemma \ref{Kollar} to
$$ \mathrm{ord}_S(Pf)\ge \mathrm{ord}_S(f)-r\left(1-\frac{n-1}{n}\min\{1,\delta(S,\Delta_S)\}\right)A_X(S).$$
One can ask whether we can prove Lemma \ref{Kollar} for all valuations, not only for Kollár components. We do not know the proof, since it heavily relies on the geometric structure of a prime divisor (for example, adjunction and the use of \cite[Lemma 5.9]{XZ26b}).

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $(X,\Delta)$ be a couple, $f:X'\to X$ a proper birational morphism of normal varieties, and $E\subseteq X'$ a prime divisor. We define
$$ A_{X,\Delta,m}(E):=1+\mathrm{ord}_E(K_{X'})-\frac{1}{m}\mathrm{ord}^{\natural}_E(m(K_X+\Delta)),$$
and
$$ A_{X,\Delta}(E):=1+\mathrm{ord}_E(K_{X'})-\mathrm{ord}_E(K_X+\Delta)=\lim_{m\to \infty}A_{X,\Delta,m}(E).$$
For a general valuation $\nu\in \mathrm{Val}_X$, we can define $A_{X,\Delta,m}(\nu)$ and $A_{X,\Delta}(\nu)$ as in \cite[Section 3.2]{BdFFU15}.

label: dFH log
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{dFH log}
Let $(X,\Delta)$ be a klt type couple, and let $\mathfrak{a}\subseteq \mathcal{O}_X$ be an ideal. We define
$$ \mathrm{lct}^{\mathrm{dFH}}(X,\Delta;\mathfrak{a}):=\inf_{\nu\in \mathrm{Val}^*_X}\frac{A_{X,\Delta}(\nu)}{\nu(\mathfrak{a})}.$$
If $\mathfrak{a}=\mathcal{O}_X(-G)$ for some effective Weil divisor $G$ on $X$, then we denote by
$$ \mathrm{lct}^{\mathrm{dFH}}(X,\Delta;G):=\mathrm{lct}^{\mathrm{dFH}}(X,\Delta;\mathcal{O}_X(-G)).$$

label: yakmulsan
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{yakmulsan}
Let $(X,\Delta)\to S$ be a family of couples, and let $S'\subseteq S$ be a Zariski-dense subset of closed points such that $(X_s,\Delta_s)$ is of klt type.

\smallskip

Suppose that there exists a positive integer $r$ such that $r(K_X+\Delta)$ is integral and a divisor $0\le rG\sim -r(K_X+\Delta)$ and a positive number $c>0$ such that $\mathrm{lct}^{\mathrm{dFH}}(X_s,\Delta_s,rG_s)>c$. Then, the geometric generic fiber of $(X,\Delta)\to S$ is of klt type.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We will use a family version of \cite[Corollary 11.2.22]{Laz04b}. We use a sub-klt pair on a log resolution rather than $(X,\Delta)$ itself to avoid an unwelcome Jacobian factor in subadditivity.

\smallskip

\noindent \textbf{Step 1.} In this step, we establish a bound of the log discrepancy $A_{X'_s,B_s}(\nu)$ with the Nakayama asymptotic order $\sigma_{\nu}$ to use the argument in \cite[Corollary 11.2.22]{Laz04b} (cf. (\ref{simple1})).

\smallskip

Let $\pi:X'\to X$ be a log resolution of $(X,\Delta,\mathcal{O}_X(-rG))$. Let $L:=\frac{1}{r}f^{\natural}(rG)$ be a $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier divisor on $X'$ such that 
\begin{equation}\label{asdf}
\mathcal{O}_X(-rG)\cdot \mathcal{O}_{X'}=\mathcal{O}_{X'}(-rL),
\end{equation}
Choose $h\in K(X)^{\times}$ such that $r(G+K_X+\Delta)=\mathrm{div}_X(h)$. Define 
\begin{equation} \label{as1}
B:=-L-K_{X'/S}+\frac{1}{r}\mathrm{div}_{X'}(h).
\end{equation}

\smallskip

We may assume that
\begin{itemize}
    \item $\mathcal{O}_X(-rG)\otimes \kappa(s)=\mathcal{O}_{X_s}(-rG_s)$ for every $s\in S$, and
    \item $\pi:X'\to X$ is a fiberwise log resolution over $S$ (for the definition of \emph{fiberwise log resolution}, see \cite[Definition-Lemma 2.8]{Xu20}).
\end{itemize}
The first comes from \cite[Corollary 10.13]{Kol23}, and the second follows from \cite[Definition-Lemma 2.8]{Xu20}.

\smallskip

By the equality (\ref{asdf}), we have a surjection
$$ \pi^*\mathcal{O}_X(-rG)\to \mathcal{O}_{X'}(-rL).$$
Tensoring $\kappa(s)$ gives a surjection.
$$ \pi^*_s\mathcal{O}_{X_s}(-rG_s)\to \mathcal{O}_{X'}(-rL)\otimes \kappa(s).$$
Since we may assume that $rL\to S$ is flat by generic flatness (cf. \cite[Proposition 052A]{Stacks}),
$$ \mathrm{Tor}^{\mathcal{O}_S}_1(\mathcal{O}_{rL},\kappa(s))=0,$$
and thus considering the exact sequence
$$ 0\to \mathcal{O}_{X'}(-rL)\to \mathcal{O}_{X'}\to \mathcal{O}_{rL}\to 0,$$
we obtain an inclusion $\mathcal{O}_{X'}(-rL)\otimes \kappa(s)\subseteq \mathcal{O}_{X'_s}$, and the image is $\mathcal{O}_{X_s}(-rL_s)$. Hence, we obtain
\begin{equation} \label{듸듸<3}
\mathcal{O}_{X_s}(-rG_s)\cdot \mathcal{O}_{X'_s}=\mathcal{O}_{X'_s}(-rL_s).
\end{equation}

\smallskip

let $m=r\ell$ for a positive integer $\ell$, and let $u\in \mathcal{O}_{X_s}(mG_s)$ be a local section. Then, $u\cdot \mathcal{O}_{X_s}(-rG_s)^{\ell}\subseteq \mathcal{O}_{X_s}$, and thus by (\ref{듸듸<3}), $u\cdot \mathcal{O}_{X'_s}(-mL_s)\subseteq \mathcal{O}_{X'_s}$. Hence, $u\in \mathcal{O}_{X'_s}(mL_s)$. Since
$$ \mathcal{O}_{X_s}(mG_s)\to (\pi_s)_*\mathcal{O}_{X'_s}(mL_s)$$
is injective, we deduce that for every $m\in r\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ and every $s\in S'$,
\begin{equation}\label{combining1} 
(\pi_s)_*\mathcal{O}_{X'_s}(mL_s)=\mathcal{O}_{X_s}(mG_s)=h^{-\frac{m}{r}}_s\mathcal{O}_{X_s}(-m(K_{X_s}+\Delta_s)).
\end{equation}
Note that the relative base ideal can be written as
\begin{equation} \label{combining2}
\begin{aligned}
\mathfrak{b}(X'_s/X_s,|mL_s|)&:=\mathrm{Im}(\pi^*_s\pi_{*s}\mathcal{O}_{X'_s}(mL_s)\otimes \mathcal{O}_{X'_s}(-mL_s)\to \mathcal{O}_{X'_s})
\\ &=\mathrm{Im}(\pi^*_s\mathcal{O}_{X_s}(mG_s)\otimes \mathcal{O}_{X'_s}(-mL_s)\to \mathcal{O}_{X'_s})
\\ &=\mathrm{Im}(\pi^*_s\mathcal{O}_{X_s}(mG_s)\to \mathcal{O}_{X'_s}(mL_s))\otimes \mathcal{O}_{X'_s}(-mL_s)
\\ &=(\mathcal{O}_{X_s}(mG_s)\cdot \mathcal{O}_{X'_s})\otimes \mathcal{O}_{X_s}(-mL_s).
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Hence, combining (\ref{combining1}) and (\ref{combining2}), we obtain
\begin{equation} \label{as2}
\sigma_{\nu,m}(X'_s/X_s,L_s)=\nu(L_s)-\frac{\nu(h_s)}{r}+\frac{1}{m}\nu(\mathcal{O}_X(-m(K_{X_s}+\Delta_s))).
\end{equation}
Thus,
\begin{equation} \label{jesan}
\begin{aligned}
A_{X_s,\Delta_s,m}(\nu)&=A_{X'_s}(\nu)+
\nu(K_{X'_s})-\frac{1}{m}\nu(\mathcal{O}_{X_s}(-m(K_{X_s}+\Delta_s))) &(1)
\\ &=A_{X'_s}(\nu)+\nu(K_{X'_s})+\nu(L_s)-\frac{\nu(h_s)}{r}-\sigma_{\nu,m}(X'_s/X_s,L_s)& (2)
\\ &=A_{X'_s,B_s}(\nu)-\sigma_{\nu,m}(X'_s/X_s,L_s), & (3)
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
where
\begin{itemize}
    \item (1) comes from the definition of $A_{X_s,\Delta_s,m}(\nu)$,
    \item (2) follows from (\ref{as2}), and
    \item (3) follows from (\ref{as1}).
\end{itemize}
Moreover, by assumption, 
\begin{equation}\label{missing}
A_{X_s,\Delta_s}(\nu)\ge c\cdot \nu^{\natural}(rG_s)\overset{(1)}{=}cr\cdot \nu(L_s)\ge cr\cdot \sigma_{\nu}(X'_s/X_s,L_s),
\end{equation}
where (1) follows from (\ref{듸듸<3}). Hence, by (\ref{jesan}),
\begin{equation} \label{simple1}
A_{X'_s,B_s}(\nu)\ge (1+cr)\cdot \sigma_{\nu}(X'_s/X_s,L_s).
\end{equation}

\smallskip

\noindent \textbf{Step 2.} In this step, using the family version of \cite[Corollary 11.2.22]{Laz04b}, we can transform $\sigma_{\nu}$ in (\ref{missing}) with $\sigma_{\nu,m}$, and hence we can use \cite[Theorem 1.2]{dFH09}. As explained above, we work with sub-klt pair of a smooth variety in order to avoid an unwelcome Jacobian factor (cf. \cite{Tak13}).

\smallskip

Let $s\in S'$. Since each $X_s$ is of klt type, $(X'_s,B_s)$ is sub-klt (cf. (\ref{jesan})). Let us prove that there exists $C>0$ that does not depend on $s,m,\nu$ such that
\begin{equation} \label{simple2}
\sigma_{\nu,m}(X'_s/X_s,L_s)\le \sigma_{\nu}(X'_s/X_s,L_s)+\frac{C}{m}A_{X'_s,B_s}(\nu).
\end{equation}
We follow the proof of \cite[Theorem 11.2.21]{Laz04b}. Indeed, let $H$ be a very ample divisor on $X'$. Then, by relative Nadel vanishing theorem (cf. \cite[Generalization 11.2.15]{Laz04b}) and Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity (cf. \cite[Example 1.8.24]{Laz04a}),
$$ \mathcal{J}(X'_s/X_s,\|mL_s\|)\otimes \mathcal{O}_{X'_s}(K_{X'_s}+(\dim X/S+1)H+mL_s)$$
is $\pi_s$-generated. Hence, there exists an effective Cartier divisor $A$ on $X'$ such that
$$ \mathcal{J}(X'_s/X_s,\|mL_s\|)\otimes \mathcal{O}_{X'_s}(-A_s)\subseteq \mathfrak{b}(X'_s/X_s,|mL_s|)$$
(cf. \cite[Theorem 11.2.21]{Laz04b}). Moreover, subadditivity states that
$$ \mathfrak{b}(X'_s/X_s,|mqL_s|)\subseteq \mathcal{J}(X'_s/X_s,\|mqL_s\|)\subseteq \mathcal{J}(X'_s/X_s,\|mL_s\|)^q\text{ for }q\ge 1$$
(cf. \cite[Corollary 11.2.4]{Laz04b}). Hence,
$$ \sigma_{\nu,m}(X'_s/X_s,L_s)\le \sigma_{\nu}(X'_s/X_s,L_s)+\frac{\nu(A_s)}{m}.$$
Finally, we can fix $\varepsilon>0$ such that $(X'_s,B_s+\varepsilon A_s)$ is sub-klt. Hence, $\nu(A_s)\le \varepsilon^{-1}A_{X'_s,B_s}(\nu)$. Put $C:=\varepsilon^{-1}$.

\smallskip

\noindent \textbf{Step 3.} Hence, we obtain
$$ 
\begin{aligned}
A_{X_s,\Delta_s,m}(\nu)&=A_{X'_s,B_s}(\nu)-\sigma_{\nu,m}(X'_s/X_s,L_s) & (1)
\\ &\ge A_{X'_s,B_s}(\nu)-\sigma_{\nu}(X'_s/X_s,L_s)-\frac{C}{m}A_{X'_s,B_s}(\nu)& (2)
\\ &\ge A_{X'_s,B_s}(\nu)-\frac{1}{1+cr}A_{X'_s,B_s}(\nu)-\frac{C}{m}A_{X'_s,B_s}(\nu) & (3)
\\ &=\left(\frac{cr}{1+cr}-\frac{C}{m}\right)A_{X'_s,B_s}(\nu),
\end{aligned}
$$
here,
\begin{itemize}
    \item (1) follows from (\ref{jesan}),
    \item (2) comes from (\ref{simple2}), and
    \item (3) is due to (\ref{simple1}).
\end{itemize}
Thus, for every sufficiently divisible $m$, $A_{X_s,\Delta_s,m}(\nu)>0$. By \cite[Corollary 10.13]{Kol23} again, after shrinking $S$, for a fixed $m$, we may assume that
$$ \mathcal{O}_X(-m(K_X+\Delta))\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_S} \kappa(s)=\mathcal{O}_{X_s}(-m(K_{X_s}+\Delta_s)).$$
Thus, by the same argument as in the proof of (\ref{듸듸<3}),
$$ A_{X_{\overline{\eta}},\Delta_{\overline{\eta}},m}(E)>0\text{ for every prime divisor }E\text{ over }X_{\overline{\eta}}.$$
Hence, \cite[Theorem 1.2]{dFH09} gives the proof.

title: Proof
body_md:
After shrinking $S$, we may assume that $X:=\operatorname{Spec} R$ is affine. Let $0\le G\sim_{\mathbb{Q},S} -K_X$ be any effective $\mathbb{Q}$-Weil divisor on $X$, $r$ be a positive integer such that $rG\sim_S -rK_X$, and let $0\ne f\in \mathcal{O}_X(-rG)\subseteq R$ be an element. After shrinking $S$ again, by generic flatness (cf. \cite[Proposition 052A]{Stacks}), we may assume that both $\mathrm{div}\,f$ and $rG$ are flat over $S$. Moreover, we obtain
$$ \mathrm{lct}^{\mathrm{dFH}}(X_s;(f_s))\le \mathrm{lct}^{\mathrm{dFH}}(X_s;rG_s)$$
for every $s\in S'$. We will prove that there exists a constant $c>0$ such that $\mathrm{lct}^{\mathrm{dFH}}(X_s;(f_s))>c$; if the proof is complete, then we have $X_{\overline{\eta}}$ is of klt type by Lemma \ref{yakmulsan}.

\smallskip

We denote the base change of $f$ to the geometric generic fiber by $f$ using an abuse of notation. Since $\mathcal{O}_{X_{\overline{\eta}}}$ is $\mathcal{D}_{X_{\overline{\eta}}}$-simple, we obtain that there exists a relative differential operator $P:\mathcal{O}_{X_{\overline{\eta}}}\to \mathcal{O}_{X_{\overline{\eta}}}$ over $S$ such that $P(f)=1$. After a generic finite base change of $S$, we obtain a differential operator $P_S:R\to R$ such that $P_S\otimes 1=P$. Moreover, $P_S(f)=1$; indeed, $P_S(f)\otimes 1=(P_S\otimes 1)(f\otimes 1)=P(f)=1$ by definition, and hence $P_S(f)=1$ since $R\to R\otimes \overline{\kappa(\eta)}, \,\,\,a\mapsto a\otimes 1$ is injective. We denote $P_s:=P_S\otimes \kappa(s)$ for $s\in S'$. Then, $P_s(f_s)=1$.

\smallskip

Let $s\in S'$. By \cite{BCHM} (cf. \cite[Theorem 92]{Kol08}), we obtain that $\bigoplus_{m\ge 0}\mathcal{O}_X(-mK_{X_s})$ is finitely generated. Set $X'(s):=\operatorname{Proj}_{\mathcal{O}_{X_s}}\bigoplus_{m\ge 0}\mathcal{O}_X(-mK_{X_s})$, and let $\pi(s):X'(s)\to X_s$ be the natural morphism. Then, we obtain that
$$ \mathcal{O}_X(-mK_{X_s})\cdot \mathcal{O}_{X'(s)}=\mathcal{O}_{X'(s)}(-mK_{X'(s)})\text{ for a sufficiently divisible }m,$$
and hence 
$$A_{X_s}(\nu')=A_{X'(s)}(\nu')\text{ for every }\nu'\in \mathrm{Val}_{X_s},$$
and
$$ \mathrm{lct}^{\mathrm{dFH}}(X_s;(f_s))=\mathrm{lct}(X'(s);(\pi(s)^*f_s)).$$
We can extend $P_s$ to $P_{X'(s)}:\mathcal{O}_{X'(s)}\to \mathcal{O}_{X'(s)}$. Now, by Lemma \ref{daljeonjeosuji}, we obtain that there exists a Kollár component $T$ over $X'(s)$ computing $\mathrm{lct}(X'(s);(\pi(s)^*f_s))$. Applying Lemma \ref{Kollar}, we obtain that
$$ 
\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{lct}^{\mathrm{dFH}}(X_s;(f_s))&=\mathrm{lct}(X'(s);(\pi(s)^*f_s))
\\ &=\frac{A_{X'(s)}(T)}{\mathrm{ord}_T(\pi(s)^*f_s)}
\\ &\ge \frac{1}{\mathrm{ord}\,P_{X'(s)}}\ge \frac{1}{\mathrm{ord}\,P}.
\end{aligned}$$
We complete the proof.

title: Remark
body_md:
One can ask whether there is a couple version of Theorem \ref{simple}. A problem is that we do not know the pair version of Lemma \ref{Kollar}. Indeed, the naive generalization of Theorem \ref{simple} 
$$\mathrm{ord}_S(Pf)\ge \mathrm{ord}_S(f)-rA_{X,\Delta}(S)$$
is false. 

\smallskip

Let $X:=\mathbb{A}^3_{\mathbb{C}}$, $D_i=(x_i=0)$ for $i=1,2,3$, and $\Delta:=\frac{5}{6}(D_1+D_2+D_3)$. Let $\pi:X'\to X$ be the blowup at the origin, and let $S$ be the exceptional divisor. Let $\Delta_{X'}$ be the strict transform of $\Delta$. Then,
$$ K_{X'}=\pi^*K_X+2S,\,\,\, \pi^*\Delta=\Delta_Y+\frac{5}{2}S,$$
and hence
$$ K_{X'}+S+\Delta_Y=\pi^*(K_X+\Delta)+\frac{1}{2}S, \,\,\, A_{X,\Delta}(S)=\frac{1}{2}.$$
Since $-S$ is $\pi$-ample, we obtain that $S$ is a Kollár component over $X$.

\smallskip

Let $P=\frac{\partial^r}{\partial^rx^r_1}$, and let $f=x^r_1$. Then, $Pf=r!$, $\mathrm{ord}_S(f)=r$, $\mathrm{ord}_S(Pf)=0$, and thus $\mathrm{ord}_S(Pf)< \mathrm{ord}_S(f)-rA_{X,\Delta}(S)$.

title: Remark
body_md: As a reduction mod $p$ analog, one may wonder whether $D$-simplicity plus strongly $F$-regular type property imply the klt type property. One problem is that there is no valuative approach in $F$-singularity theory (cf. \cite[4.3. Positive characteristics]{XZ26a}).
